data.name: Tutorial_P0_Body
data.value:
RemEx turns your PC into a secure remote command center. From your phone you can monitor hardware sensors, launch apps, manage files and processes, and stream your desktop.
RemEx runs on this PC and your phone connects to it. Every connection is protected with TLS plus PIN-based pairing.

data.name: Tutorial_P1_Body1
data.value: This desktop app includes an embedded RemEx PC that starts automatically. Your Android phone connects to it — not the other way around.

data.name: Tutorial_P1_Body2
data.value: RemEx starts automatically when you sign in to this PC — a logon task on Windows, an autostart entry on Linux — so your phone can connect whenever you are signed in. Sensor monitoring and power commands keep working when the screen locks, but streaming or controlling the desktop needs the session unlocked. If the PC is switched off or signed out, wake it with Wake-on-LAN and sign in first.

data.name: Tutorial_P4_Body1
data.value: For detailed hardware monitoring (300+ sensors), install HWiNFO64 — it's free for personal use.

data.name: Tutorial_P4_Steps
data.value: 1. Download from hwinfo.com 2. Run HWInfo → Settings (⚙) → Main Settings 3. Check 'Shared Memory Support' → OK 4. HWInfo must be running for RemEx to read its sensors

data.name: Tutorial_P4_Warning
data.value: ⚠ HWInfo's Shared Memory auto-disables after 12 hours (free version). Re-enable it periodically, or consider the Pro license.

data.name: Tutorial_P5_HWInfo
data.value: 🟢 HWInfo: 300+ sensors — CPU temps, GPU clocks, fan speeds, voltages, power draw. Requires HWInfo running.

data.name: Tutorial_P5_BuiltIn
data.value: 🪟 Built-in: Basic sensors — CPU usage, RAM, disk I/O, network rates. Always available, no extra software.

data.name: Tutorial_P5_Body2
data.value: Pin your favorite sensors to the Home screen from Settings → Pinned Sensors.

data.name: Tutorial_P6_Body1
data.value: The App Launcher lets you start programs on your PC from your phone. Apps must be configured here first.

data.name: Tutorial_P6_Steps
data.value: 1. Navigate to the Launcher page (sidebar) 2. Click '+ Add Program' 3. Browse to the .exe or shortcut 4. Launch from your Android app!

data.name: Tutorial_P6_Note
data.value: Your phone can only start programs you add here — for safety, RemEx won't launch anything that isn't on this list.

data.name: Tutorial_P7_Body1
data.value: Your Android app finds this PC automatically using mDNS. Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi / LAN.

data.name: Tutorial_P7_Body2
data.value: If auto-discovery doesn't work, find your PC's IP manually:

data.name: Tutorial_P7_IpSteps
data.value: Windows: CMD → ipconfig → 'IPv4 Address' Linux: ip addr or hostname -I

data.name: Tutorial_P7_Body3
data.value: Then enter the IP address and port in the Android app. If this device is not paired yet, enter the 6-digit PIN shown on the PC.

data.name: Tutorial_P8_QR_Body1
data.value: The fastest way to connect your phone is by scanning a QR code. The PC generates a pairing code that contains everything your mobile app needs.

data.name: Tutorial_P8_QR_Steps
data.value: 1. Open Settings → Connection on the PC 2. Click "Show QR Code" 3. Open the RemEx mobile app 4. Tap the QR scanner icon on the connection screen 5. Point your camera at the code — you'll connect automatically!

data.name: Tutorial_P8_QR_Body2
data.value: No typing, no IP addresses — just scan and go. The connection details are saved so you only need to scan once.

data.name: About_WhatsNew_Features_Body
data.value: Hardware-accelerated remote desktop via NVENC, QSV, AMF, or VAAPI on the PC. Android decodes with MediaCodec for zero-copy GPU delivery. Falls back to MJPEG automatically when hardware encoders are unavailable.

data.name: About_WhatsNew_Fixes_Body
data.value: All traffic is encrypted with TLS 1.3 where the client supports it, and never below TLS 1.2. First-time pairing uses ECDH P-256 key exchange with a 6-digit PIN — no plaintext keys ever on the wire. The client pins the PC's SHA-256 certificate fingerprint for all future connections.

data.name: About_WhatsNew_FileTransfer_Body
data.value: Browse the PC's shared folders and transfer files in either direction with SHA-256 integrity verification. Android can share its own folders back to the PC. Transfers show live progress with cancel support.

data.name: About_WhatsNew_Android_Body
data.value: Material 3 Expressive with spring physics throughout — list reorder, pull-to-refresh, app tiles, animated gauges. 8 Quick Settings tiles for one-tap power commands. Resizable home screen widgets. Two-stage haptic feedback. Target SDK 37 (Android 17).

data.name: About_WhatsNew_Issues_Body
data.value: First-class Linux support with native PipeWire capture, full Wayland input injection, and autostart at sign-in. New premium launcher icon, Cosmic Zoom boot animation, colorful ANSI startup banner, and canvas clipboard bitmap copy.

data.name: Faq_Q1_Question
data.value: What do I need to run on my PC?

data.name: Faq_Q1_Answer
data.value: You need RemEx running on your PC — it's a single app (remex.agent) that runs elevated in your signed-in session and starts automatically at sign-in. Download the latest installer from GitHub Releases, run it, and it's ready before you pair.

data.name: Faq_Q2_Question
data.value: How do I pair my phone?

data.name: Faq_Q2_Answer
data.value: Open Settings → Connection in this window to show a QR code and a 6-digit pairing PIN. On your phone, open the RemEx app and scan the QR code for the fastest setup, or enter the PIN when the app asks. Pairing always happens from the phone to this PC.

data.name: Faq_Q3_Question
data.value: How do I find my PC's IP address?

data.name: Faq_Q3_Answer
data.value: Windows: 'ipconfig' in Command Prompt. macOS: System Settings -> Network. Linux: 'ip addr' in terminal. You can also see the IP directly in the RemEx window on your PC.

data.name: Faq_Q4_Question
data.value: Auto-discovery isn't finding my PC. What should I check?

data.name: Faq_Q4_Answer
data.value: 1. Make sure RemEx is running on your PC. 2. Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi / LAN. 3. On Android 13+, allow Nearby devices; on Android 17+, allow Local Network access too. 4. Check whether your router has AP/Client Isolation enabled. 5. Corporate or guest networks often block mDNS discovery.

data.name: Faq_Q5_Answer
data.value: The default port is 5005. If it is busy, RemEx tries the next free port instead — 5006, 5007 and so on, up to 5009. You can see the active port in the RemEx window on your PC.

data.name: Faq_Q6_Question
data.value: Can I connect over the internet?

data.name: Faq_Q6_Answer
data.value: RemEx is designed for local network (LAN) use. For secure remote access from anywhere, we recommend Tailscale — a zero-configuration WireGuard® VPN that connects your devices without port forwarding or exposing your PC to the internet. Port forwarding is not recommended for security reasons.

data.name: Faq_Q7_Question
data.value: Remote Desktop is laggy. What can I do?

data.name: Faq_Q7_Answer
data.value: • Lower the Quality slider. • Reduce Target FPS — 15-20 is usually plenty. • Lower the Scale. • Use a fast local network. 5 GHz Wi-Fi or a wired connection is best — this is the most common cause of lag. • You don't need to set up screen capture. RemEx picks the fastest method your PC supports, automatically.

data.name: Faq_Q8_Answer
data.value: Wake-on-LAN lets you power on your PC remotely. Enable it in your BIOS/UEFI and network adapter properties. Then enter your PC's MAC address in the Connection screen.

data.name: Faq_Q9_Answer
data.value: Open File Transfer from the sidebar or command palette. You'll only see the folders the PC has shared, and writable roots accept uploads while read-only roots stay download-only.

data.name: Faq_Q10_Question
data.value: Can I lock my PC remotely?

data.name: Faq_Q10_Answer
data.value: Yes. Use the Remote Control screen or command palette on desktop, or add the Lock PC Quick Settings tile on Android for one-tap access.

data.name: Faq_Q11_Question
data.value: How do I set up Tailscale for remote access?

data.name: Faq_Q11_Answer
data.value: 1. Install Tailscale on your PC: tailscale.com/download (Windows) or run: curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh (Linux). 2. Sign in and connect: follow the browser prompt (Windows) or run: sudo tailscale up (Linux). 3. Install Tailscale on Android from the Play Store and sign in with the same account. 4. Find your PC's Tailscale IP (starts with 100.x.y.z) in the Tailscale app or at login.tailscale.com. 5. Enter that IP in RemEx's Connection screen — you can now connect securely from anywhere.

data.name: Tutorial_P2_Body1
data.value: To keep RemEx running 24/7 without being logged in, install it as a Windows service:

data.name: Tutorial_P2_Steps
data.value: 1. Open Settings (⚙) → scroll to 'Windows Service' 2. Set your Windows username and password 3. Click 'Install as Service' 4. The service starts automatically on boot

data.name: Tutorial_P2_Note
data.value: The service runs under your user account so it can access your desktop session for screen capture and app launching.

data.name: Tutorial_P3_Body1
data.value: On Linux, RemEx PC installs as a user-level systemd service so it can start with your session and stay available in the background.

data.name: Tutorial_P3_Steps
data.value: 1. Download the latest Linux PC archive from GitHub Releases. 2. Extract it. 3. Run ./install.sh install inside the remex-PC folder. 4. Use systemctl --user status remex-PC to verify it is running.

data.name: Tutorial_P3_Link
data.value: Tip: use the bundled install.sh script instead of copying service files by hand.

data.name: Tutorial_P3_Body2
data.value: The same release page also includes the Linux desktop client package if you want the full Avalonia UI on that machine.

data.name: Faq_Q12_Question
data.value: My phone suddenly refuses to connect and asks to pair again. Why?

data.name: Faq_Q12_Answer
data.value: When your phone first pairs, it remembers this PC's exact security certificate fingerprint and will only ever trust that certificate again. If the certificate changes — for example after reinstalling RemEx, restoring this PC from a backup, or moving to new hardware — the phone refuses the connection instead of trusting a potential impostor. This is expected security behavior, not a bug. To fix it, remove (unpair) this PC in the phone app's Connection screen, then pair again with the QR code or new 6-digit PIN shown in this window.

data.name: Faq_Q13_Question
data.value: Why does RemEx need special permission to run?

data.name: Faq_Q13_Answer
data.value: RemEx keeps a security certificate that your phone uses to recognize this PC. It is stored where nothing else can read it, so no other program — and nobody else signed in to this PC — can copy it and pretend to be your PC. If RemEx cannot read that file it still opens but cannot accept connections, so your phone cannot reach it even though it still shows as paired. Windows: RemEx needs administrator rights, because only administrators can read that protected file. It normally starts with administrator rights on its own when you sign in, so this should be rare — but if your phone cannot connect, close RemEx, right-click it, choose "Run as administrator" and try again. Linux: RemEx does not need root, and you should never start it with sudo. The certificate sits in your own home folder, readable only by you. If your phone cannot connect, an old 'remex-host' install has probably left the certificate owned by root; run the RemEx installer again and it will repair that for you. Either way your paired phones keep working — the certificate itself never changes.

data.name: Faq_Q14_Question
data.value: How do I stop RemEx starting automatically when I sign in?

data.name: Faq_Q14_Answer
data.value: Open Settings and turn off "Launch RemEx when you sign in". That is all most people need: RemEx stays installed and you can still start it yourself whenever you want, and switching it back on restores automatic startup. Behind that switch, Windows uses a Task Scheduler task named "RemEx" — you can see it in Task Scheduler under Task Scheduler Library — and Linux uses an autostart entry at ~/.config/autostart/remex-agent.desktop. If RemEx ever stops starting at sign-in, switch the setting off and back on to recreate it.
